boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of California-Riverside, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend sequence that orients you to UCR landmarks, campus resources, recreation, and nearby UCR ARTS.

cards.title: Start with a campus tour
cards.subtitle: Undergraduate Admissions
cards.notes: Reserve a daily prospective-student tour, then use its overview of campus colleges, culture, and resources to plan the rest of your weekend.
cards.short_summary: A structured first look at the campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UCR offers daily campus tours for prospective students, including an optional admissions presentation.
cards.access_notes: Prospective-student tours require a reservation; the page says guests may bring up to four people.

cards.title: Get your bearings at the Bell Tower
cards.subtitle: Carillon Mall, UC Riverside
cards.notes: Pause at this central landmark, take a photo from the surrounding mall, and use it as a simple reference point before exploring nearby buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bell Tower was built in 1965–66 and contains a 48-bell carillon.
cards.source_title: Highlander History — UC Riverside Student Life
cards.access_notes: View the outdoor landmark from the surrounding campus paths.

cards.title: Listen for a carillon recital
cards.subtitle: UCR Bell Tower
cards.notes: If your weekend extends into Monday, stop near the tower at noon to hear the recurring live carillon performance during the academic year.
cards.short_summary: A recurring live-bell performance at the tower.
cards.evidence_claim: UCR Student Life says live Bell Tower performances occur weekly on Mondays at noon during the academic year, with few exceptions.
cards.source_title: Highlander History — UC Riverside Student Life
cards.access_notes: Academic-year schedule; confirm the events calendar before going because exceptions can occur.

cards.title: Find the library’s first-floor hub
cards.subtitle: Tomás Rivera Library
cards.notes: Walk through the first floor to locate community computers, study areas, and the building entrance you can use as a reliable campus meetup point.
cards.evidence_claim: UCR Library reports that Tomás Rivera Library has community computers on its first floor that do not require authentication.
cards.source_title: Library Desktop Computers Get an Upgrade
cards.access_notes: Community computers are open-access; building access and hours can vary, so check the library before visiting.

cards.title: Locate Orbach’s community computers
cards.subtitle: Raymond L. Orbach Science Library
cards.notes: Make a quick pass through the first floor to note a science-library option for study time, printing plans, or a future research session.
cards.short_summary: A second library stop with open-access computers.
cards.evidence_claim: UCR Library reports that Orbach Library has community computers on its first floor that do not require authentication.
cards.source_title: Library Desktop Computers Get an Upgrade
cards.access_notes: Community computers are open-access; confirm current building hours before making a dedicated trip.

cards.title: Take a lap through the SRC
cards.subtitle: UC Riverside Student Recreation Center
cards.notes: Check the current schedule, then use an open-recreation slot for a casual activity or simply learn where the courts, pool, and recreation services are.
cards.short_summary: UCR’s recreation facility and activity base.
cards.evidence_claim: All UCR students are automatically members of the Student Recreation Center, which supports exercise, sports, events, and recreation.
cards.access_notes: The SRC posts weekend hours and advises visitors to check its current schedule and closures before arrival.

cards.title: Try an open-recreation window
cards.subtitle: Student Recreation Center (SRC)
cards.notes: Use the schedule to find an available court or multipurpose room, then bring suitable activity clothes and ask the front counter about current availability.
cards.evidence_claim: UCR Open Recreation offers members and guests non-structured activities in multipurpose rooms, courts, and other spaces on a first-come basis.
cards.access_notes: Availability changes with events; UCR directs visitors to check the day’s schedule or closures before going.

cards.title: Walk the Botanic Gardens
cards.subtitle: UC Riverside east campus
cards.notes: Set aside time for an unhurried garden walk, take only permitted photos, and use the garden’s own visitor information to plan your route and timing.
cards.short_summary: A planted landscape on UCR’s east campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UCR’s long-range development plan identifies the UCR Botanic Gardens in the southeastern area of East Campus.
cards.source_title: UC Riverside 2021 Long Range Development Plan Draft EIR
cards.access_notes: Check the gardens’ visitor information for current entry guidance and any closures before heading over.

cards.title: Make an UCR ARTS museum stop
cards.subtitle: 3824 Main Street, downtown Riverside
cards.notes: Browse the current exhibition at the California Museum of Photography, then give yourself time to look around the Culver Center area before returning to campus.
cards.short_summary: A downtown UCR ARTS exhibition stop.
cards.evidence_claim: UCR ARTS lists the California Museum of Photography among its visitor locations and says UCR students with ID receive free museum admission.
cards.access_notes: Academic-year public hours are Thursday–Friday 12–5 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; UCR student ID is required for free admission.

cards.title: Plan an insect-collection visit
cards.subtitle: Entomology Research Museum, UC Riverside
cards.notes: Email ahead if you want help identifying an insect, and look for the public display cases in or near the building rather than expecting a standard gallery.
cards.short_summary: A research collection with limited public viewing.
cards.evidence_claim: The Entomology Research Museum welcomes visits by appointment and notes that public display cases in its building and the nearby department building are open to viewing.
cards.access_notes: Contact the museum before a visit; it states that it does not operate as a typical public-display museum.
